editorNote: The week reads like a dealer counter after Winter CES: Commodore, Texas Instruments, Mattel, Timex, and Spectravideo chase low-cost home buyers while IBM PC software keeps making the office machine harder to ignore.
morningLine: Home-computer makers are crowding the price cards, Lotus 1-2-3 is still the desk-side conversation, and Tootsie holds the box-office crown as Africa takes over radio.

lead.headline: Home-computer race spills from CES to store counters
lead.summary: Reports from January 1983 show a packed home-computer field after Winter CES: Commodore showed portable C64 ideas, Texas Instruments pushed a low-cost TI-99/2, Mattel promoted Aquarius, Timex brought a Spectrum-derived machine toward North America, and Spectravideo pitched a cartridge-friendly microcomputer.

computerItems.title: Commodore pushes both low-cost and portable stories
computerItems.summary: Commodore had the VIC-20 milestone and C64 momentum on one side, while CES reports described portable C64-family machines such as the SX-64/SX-100 concept for buyers who wanted a luggable color computer.

computerItems.title: Mattel Aquarius courts budget home users
computerItems.summary: Mattel Electronics demonstrated the Aquarius at Winter CES with a Z80A processor, 4K RAM, and an expected $200 price, linking the toy-and-game aisle to the home-computer shelf.

computerItems.title: TI aims below the usual computer price
computerItems.summary: Texas Instruments announced the TI-99/2 at Winter CES as a simplified, low-cost machine expected around $100, a signal of how fiercely companies were chasing first-time home buyers.

computerItems.title: Lotus keeps the IBM PC in office talk
computerItems.summary: Lotus 1-2-3, shipped in late January for MS-DOS, remained the week's serious software story by tying spreadsheet, charting, and database features to the IBM PC.

briefs.headline: Africa reaches No. 1
briefs.summary: Toto's Africa topped the Billboard Hot 100 dated February 5, 1983, with Men at Work's Down Under at No. 2.

briefs.headline: Tootsie passes $100 million
briefs.summary: For the February 4-6 domestic weekend, Tootsie stayed No. 1 and crossed $100 million in total gross.

briefs.headline: The Entity opens in second

periodAd.headline: Home Computer Price Fight
periodAd.summary: Aquarius around $200, TI aiming near $100, Timex/Sinclair 2000 at $149, and Spectravideo at $300. Ask the dealer what plugs into your television.

market.headline: Low-price micros chase the living room
market.summary: January CES announcements show manufacturers using price, cartridge compatibility, and bundled BASIC to pull families toward home computers, while business buyers keep watching IBM PC software.
